title: Do not let grief turn into ownership
summary: The shabad honors the ache but breaks the cry of 'mine.' Grief becomes clearer when the soul is returned to Hukam, one dust, one light, one breath.
takeaway: Let sorrow bow before the soul becomes possession.
lifeApplication: When panic reaches for the word mine, breathe with the line about one dust and one light. Grieve without claiming what Hukam never gave you to own.

source.shortMeaning: Possessive grief is unsettled by Hukam: the soul belongs to the One, not to our claim.
source.lifeApplication: In the first rise of panic, release the word mine and breathe beneath Hukam.

evidence.coreClaim: Possessive grief is unsettled by Hukam: the soul belongs to the One, not to our claim.
evidence.turn: The ache remains honest, but ownership loses its authority over the soul.
